source: 12 Fortinet feature/admin guide lessons; Community secondary scenario context

questions.stem: A hub negotiates IKE_SA_INIT, but a new tunnel stalls before IKE_AUTH after enabling PQC. Which comparison is decisive?

choices.text: Compare both peers' phase-1 additional KE groups and exchange support.
choices.feedback: IKE_INTERMEDIATE proposals must agree before authentication can finish.

choices.text: Compare firewall policy sequence numbers on the inside interfaces.
choices.feedback: Forward policy ordering does not negotiate additional IKE keys.

choices.text: Compare ESP traffic counters after clearing the active tunnel.
choices.feedback: ESP counters are downstream and may remain zero after negotiation fails.

choices.text: Compare DNS resolver cache entries for the peer hostname.
choices.feedback: DNS cache may affect reachability but not a negotiated KE mismatch.

questions.stem: IKEv2 is established, but a new CHILD_SA fails following phase-2 PQC changes. Where should diagnosis start?

choices.text: Review both phase-2 addke proposals and FOLLOWUP_KE behavior.
choices.feedback: CHILD_SA rekey/additional KE can differ from the established IKE SA.

choices.text: Review the FortiGate's global web proxy certificate settings.
choices.feedback: Proxy certificates do not determine CHILD_SA additional KE compatibility.

choices.text: Review the switch's 802.1X port authorization counters.
choices.feedback: 802.1X controls local access rather than IKE phase-2 negotiation.

choices.text: Review the FortiAnalyzer report retention and roll schedule.
choices.feedback: Log retention cannot cause a phase-2 KEM proposal mismatch.

questions.stem: A tunnel's ESP counters increase after a PQC rollout. What is still unproven?

choices.text: Whether the firewall rule permits all production destinations.
choices.feedback: ESP counts alone do not prove every destination policy.

choices.text: Whether the negotiated SA used the intended additional KEM.
choices.feedback: Data-plane counters cannot attest to the negotiated addke group.

choices.text: Whether the peer can route return traffic through the tunnel.
choices.feedback: ESP counts alone do not show return-path reachability.

choices.text: Whether the WAN MTU can carry ordinary encrypted packets.
choices.feedback: Packets can pass without proving all larger MTU cases.

questions.stem: An engineer wants to enable PQC on seven spoke tunnels in one change. Which staged test best reduces negotiation risk?

choices.text: Increase DPD retries and assume KEM compatibility follows.
choices.feedback: DPD timing does not establish cryptographic group support.

choices.text: Enable all additional KE rounds on every spoke immediately.
choices.feedback: A simultaneous rollout hides which peer proposal first fails.

choices.text: Test a compatible pair, verify exchanges, then stage spokes.
choices.feedback: A pilot verifies compatibility and rekey behavior before scale.

choices.text: Enable only ESP encryption changes and skip peer checks.
choices.feedback: ESP cipher changes do not verify IKE additional exchanges.

questions.stem: FortiManager shows no DHCP Discover in a scheduled FortiSwitch PCAP. What should be checked first?

choices.text: Selected switch, ingress port, filter and capture time window.
choices.feedback: An empty capture is ambiguous until observation scope and time are correct.

choices.text: FortiAnalyzer's archive file rolling interval and quota.
choices.feedback: Archive retention does not determine FortiSwitch capture visibility.

choices.text: The WAN SD-WAN SLA target and FortiGuard license.
choices.feedback: WAN probe entitlement is unrelated to a local switch capture.

choices.text: The wireless MPSK profile's SAE transition security type.
choices.feedback: MPSK mode is not the first explanation for a mis-scoped PCAP.

questions.stem: A FortiManager capture contains RADIUS Access-Accept for a wired endpoint. What cannot yet be concluded?

choices.text: The access switch installed the authorized VLAN on its port.
choices.feedback: An Access-Accept does not prove hardware VLAN assignment.

choices.text: The RADIUS server returned an affirmative authentication decision.
choices.feedback: The packet directly shows the RADIUS response decision.

choices.text: The management workflow captured a packet at that interface.
choices.feedback: The observed packet confirms capture operation at that point.

choices.text: The upstream path carried a response toward the access switch.
choices.feedback: The observed packet supports upstream response transport.

questions.stem: An intermittent outage occurs only at 03:00. Which FortiManager capability most directly preserves evidence?

choices.text: A FortiGate firewall policy comparison from last week.
choices.feedback: Policy diffs cannot show which frames arrived at 03:00.

choices.text: A scheduled switch packet capture covering the outage.
choices.feedback: Scheduled PCAPs observe transient traffic during the failure window.

choices.text: An ADOM object deletion report after the outage.
choices.feedback: Object deletion history does not capture the transient packet path.

choices.text: A full FortiAnalyzer backup performed during business hours.
choices.feedback: A backup does not record the packet exchange causing the outage.

questions.stem: A FortiManager PCAP shows DHCP Discover but no Offer. What is the next sound isolation step?

choices.text: Replace all client MPSK keys across the WLAN.
choices.feedback: Rotating WLAN keys is unrelated to an observed DHCP Discover.

choices.text: Clear the FortiSIEM ClickHouse event database.
choices.feedback: SIEM event storage does not affect DHCP server replies.

choices.text: Capture at the uplink or FortiGate DHCP boundary.
choices.feedback: Moving the capture boundary localizes where the reply disappears.

choices.text: Immediately disable the FortiGate's DoS anomaly policy.
choices.feedback: DoS policy is unproven and may not govern this VLAN.

questions.stem: FortiAnalyzer reports archive data older than its 90-day setting. Which mechanism explains this?

choices.text: File-level retention waits until all records are out of window.
choices.feedback: Mixed-age rolled files remain until the entire file is eligible.

choices.text: Each individual archive record is deleted at midnight.
choices.feedback: Archive deletion is file-granular, not per-record at midnight.

choices.text: A report SQL dataset overrides archive deletion dates.
choices.feedback: Report datasets cannot alter archive file deletion granularity.

choices.text: The log forwarding connector always duplicates old records.
choices.feedback: Forwarding may copy logs but does not explain file eligibility.

questions.stem: An ADOM's log rate is normal but a historical report lacks one day. What does rate evidence prove?

choices.text: Current log ingestion exists, not continuous historical retention.
choices.feedback: The command observes current ADOM ingestion, not file retention.

choices.text: All historical archive files remain present and searchable.
choices.feedback: Current rate cannot attest to old archive completeness.

choices.text: All log files have been rolled precisely every 24 hours.
choices.feedback: Daily rolling must be separately configured and verified.

choices.text: The report's SQL query has no time-filter defects.
choices.feedback: A rate counter does not validate report query filters.

questions.stem: A low-volume ADOM has compressed files spanning several days. Which change targets deletion granularity?

choices.text: Increase the file size threshold to several gigabytes.
choices.feedback: Larger files generally span more days at low volume.

choices.text: Configure scheduled daily rolling for bounded file spans.
choices.feedback: Daily rolling keeps files near day boundaries for retention.

choices.text: Disable analytics indexing while keeping archive unchanged.
choices.feedback: Indexing does not change file-level archive roll boundaries.

choices.text: Move the ADOM to a different FortiManager workspace.
choices.feedback: FortiManager workspaces are unrelated to FAZ archive files.

questions.stem: Storage-size pressure removes logs from days 60–89 while day 90 survives. Why might that occur?

choices.text: A new report dataset created a gap in the raw logs.
choices.feedback: Datasets cannot create archive retention gaps by themselves.

choices.text: FortiAnalyzer automatically replays missing archived days.
choices.feedback: Retention does not automatically replay missing log history.

choices.text: Whole-file deletion follows the oldest last-received log.
choices.feedback: Deleting whole files can leave non-contiguous date coverage.

choices.text: Every record is deleted in strict chronological timestamp order.
choices.feedback: The deletion unit is a file, not an individual record.

questions.stem: A FortiSwitch ingress ACL appears in configuration but packets still pass. What evidence matters next?

choices.text: Assigned ACL group, hardware usage, action and match counters.
choices.feedback: Hardware enforcement requires attachment, support and matching action.

choices.text: FortiGate's central NAT policy and translated address pool.
choices.feedback: Central NAT does not program a FortiSwitch ingress ACL.

choices.text: FortiAnalyzer's report scheduling and analytics disk quota.
choices.feedback: Reporting storage is downstream of switch hardware decisions.

choices.text: FortiSASE administrator comments for last month's edits.
choices.feedback: Audit comments do not prove switch ASIC policy installation.

questions.stem: An ACL match counter rises but traffic is not blocked. Which explanation fits the evidence?

choices.text: The matching ACL action may count or remark, not drop.
choices.feedback: A match can trigger non-drop actions such as counting or remarking.

choices.text: The ACL must be acting as a FortiGate firewall policy.
choices.feedback: A switch ACL is not a FortiGate forwarding policy.

choices.text: The switch's MCLAG heartbeat necessarily went down.
choices.feedback: MCLAG failure is not implied by ACL counter behavior.

choices.text: The client must have received a different MPSK key.
choices.feedback: MPSK key assignment does not determine wired ACL action.

questions.stem: A switch in ACL density mode loses free entries after deleting rules. What is the documented remedy boundary?

choices.text: Change the FortiManager ADOM's policy revision status.
choices.feedback: ADOM revisions do not release switch density-mode allocation.

choices.text: Plan ACL key-compaction or switch restart with disruption awareness.
choices.feedback: Density-mode hardware resources may need compaction or restart.

choices.text: Run FortiNAC portal Publish to reload all access rules.
choices.feedback: FortiNAC web rules do not reclaim switch ACL hardware.

choices.text: Disable the FortiGate's IPsec childless IKE negotiation.
choices.feedback: IKE negotiation has no bearing on ACL TCAM reclamation.

questions.stem: A managed FortiSwitch supports ingress ACLs but a configured action fails on one model. What is most likely?

choices.text: The RADIUS shared secret must be regenerated first.
choices.feedback: RADIUS secrets are unrelated to a hardware ACL action.

choices.text: The DHCP relay agent is suppressing policy download.
choices.feedback: DHCP relay does not govern switch ACL ASIC capability.

choices.text: The model-specific ACL feature matrix restricts that action.
choices.feedback: The guide explicitly documents model-specific classifier/action limits.

choices.text: All switches support identical actions after FortiManager install.
choices.feedback: ACL action support differs by switch family and release.

questions.stem: Two MPSK clients associate to one SSID but land in different VLANs. What determines that split?

choices.text: The matched MPSK key/group's dynamic VLAN configuration.
choices.feedback: MPSK maps matched credentials to group/VLAN authorization.

choices.text: The FortiAnalyzer archive retention policy for each client.
choices.feedback: Log retention has no role in WLAN VLAN assignment.

choices.text: The SD-WAN rule's chosen underlay health-check target.
choices.feedback: WAN health checks occur after local WLAN segmentation.

choices.text: The FortiPAM secret checkout duration for the administrator.
choices.feedback: PAM checkout does not select client WLAN VLANs.

questions.stem: After enabling MPSK, a legacy client loses DHCP although association succeeds. Which path is most relevant?

choices.text: The key-selected VLAN's tagging, DHCP and policy path.
choices.feedback: MPSK enables dynamic VLAN; L3 reachability must be revalidated.

choices.text: The FortiGate's IKEv2 additional KE group proposal.
choices.feedback: IKE KEM negotiation is unrelated to WLAN DHCP.

choices.text: The FortiSIEM region's ClickHouse shard placement.
choices.feedback: SIEM storage placement does not provide DHCP service.

choices.text: The FortiAuthenticator OAuth token refresh expiry value.
choices.feedback: OAuth refresh tokens do not determine WPA association VLANs.

questions.stem: An SSID is configured for WPA3 SAE-only keys, but an older WPA2 client fails. Which mismatch should be examined?

choices.text: FortiManager's scheduled switch capture duration.
choices.feedback: Capture duration does not change client cipher capability.

choices.text: The MPSK security mode versus the client's WPA capability.
choices.feedback: SAE-only key types may exclude WPA2-only supplicants.

choices.text: FortiAnalyzer's compressed log file roll trigger.
choices.feedback: Archive roll triggers do not control WLAN authentication.

choices.text: FortiSASE's required administrator change-summary field.
choices.feedback: Audit comments do not change WPA3 key negotiation.

questions.stem: A team assigns two MPSK profiles to one VAP and expects both to apply. What is the documented limit?

choices.text: Both profiles apply if they share the same security type.
choices.feedback: Matching security types do not bypass the one-profile limit.

choices.text: The controller merges profiles after the next FortiAP reboot.
choices.feedback: A reboot does not change the VAP association model.

choices.text: Only one MPSK profile can be bound to a VAP.
choices.feedback: The guide explicitly restricts VAPs to one MPSK profile.

choices.text: Two profiles combine only when DHCP snooping is enabled.
choices.feedback: DHCP snooping does not merge MPSK profiles.

questions.stem: A FortiNAC portal rule was edited but browsers still follow the old redirect. What was likely omitted?

choices.text: Publishing the rule set to restart the portal HTTP process.
choices.feedback: Stored edits are not active until portal rules are published.

choices.text: Updating the FortiGate's SD-WAN FortiGuard preset database.
choices.feedback: SD-WAN presets do not change captive portal HTTP routing.

choices.text: Rebuilding the FortiSwitch ingress ACL hardware key table.
choices.feedback: Switch ACL key compaction is unrelated to portal redirects.

choices.text: Refreshing FortiSIEM's ClickHouse shard membership map.
choices.feedback: SIEM storage regions do not affect the portal HTTP process.

questions.stem: A FortiNAC request matcher uses `example.com` as regex. What subtle problem can arise?

choices.text: The dot can match any character without escaping.
choices.feedback: Unescaped dot matches any single character in regex.

choices.text: It automatically matches only exact hostname bytes.
choices.feedback: Regex dot is not an exact literal by default.

choices.text: It can only match an HTTP User Agent, never a URI.
choices.feedback: Rules can match Request URI or HTTP User Agent.

choices.text: It is interpreted as a RADIUS attribute rather than regex.
choices.feedback: Request Processing Rules inspect HTTP fields, not RADIUS attributes.

questions.stem: A portal shows 102 Request Processing Rules instead of 51. What first action is justified?

choices.text: Disable portal service logging and restart the appliance.
choices.feedback: Disabling logs removes evidence without finding duplicates.

choices.text: Identify duplicate matcher/action/target groups before changes.
choices.feedback: Grouping rule fields exposes duplicates for controlled remediation.

choices.text: Delete half the records using an unreviewed SQL command.
choices.feedback: Unreviewed database deletion risks portal configuration integrity.

choices.text: Replace all registration VLANs to clear stale browser cache.
choices.feedback: VLAN changes do not resolve duplicated portal HTTP rules.

questions.stem: A captive portal's HTTP request is redirected correctly but endpoint registration fails. What is the correct inference?

choices.text: The FortiAnalyzer report database must be out of sync.
choices.feedback: FortiAnalyzer reporting does not control registration workflow.

choices.text: The client has certainly completed all post-login compliance checks.
choices.feedback: The browser redirect is earlier than compliance completion.

choices.text: HTTP request routing works; inspect downstream registration stages.
choices.feedback: The request-rule layer can succeed while registration later fails.

choices.text: The portal HTTP rules also proved RADIUS VLAN authorization.
choices.feedback: A redirect does not prove access policy or registration success.
